COLORS LESSON · COLORS & SHADES · AGES 2–5 YEARS

Navy — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson teaches navy — blue gone dark, the color named after the sailors who wore it.

What is this?

Navy is a very dark shade of blue — the color of the whale, the moon, the bow tie and the cap on the card. It is blue with a little black stirred in: the color of the sky when the last light leaves.

What does it mean?

Navy is the only color on the shelf named after PEOPLE AT WORK: the NAVY — sailors everywhere wear dark blue uniforms, so dark blue took the name. A color with a job history.

What does the child need to know?

The child needs to: say "navy", name the recipe (blue + a little black), and pair it with the light blue card — the two ends of the blue family, day and night.

Why this matters

Navy versus light blue is the deepest compare-and-contrast in the deck: SAME color family, OPPOSITE ends. Spotting "both are blue!" is classification — the real reading-readiness skill.

What it teaches

Comparing shades within one family, a word-history story (color names come from somewhere — navy from sailors), and night-and-day reasoning.

Words to learn

navysailoruniformwhalemoonbow tiecapdarknightdeep

Say this to your child

“"Navy! Blue gone dark — night blue. The whale is navy, the moon is navy, the bow tie is navy, the cap is navy. Navy is named after the NAVY — the sailors! Their uniforms were this blue, so the color took their name."”

Step by step

  1. Three blues in a row: light blue, blue, navy — the blue family from day to night. Point and name each; the middle card is the parent and the other two are its children.
  2. The recipe: navy is blue PLUS A LITTLE BLACK. Careful with the word "little" — one extra drop and you are in black. Recipes teach precision.
  3. The name story: sailors in the NAVY wear navy uniforms in every country’s fleet — the color took its name from the people. What would YOUR uniform color be called?
  4. Square talk: the whale dives deep where it is dark, the moon comes out when the sky turns navy, the bow tie and cap are the fancy navy clothes. Sea, sky, clothes — navy works nights and weddings.
  5. Close with the moon: find the moon out the window tonight if you can. If it is a crescent, say hello from the card.

Look closer at the picture

The whale on this card is navy, and the whale on the BLUE card is bright blue — same animal, two times of day. Ask which whale swims at night. That question IS the lesson.

Ask your child

"What two colors make navy?" (blue plus a little black) "What is navy named after?" (the navy — sailors!) "Which navy thing comes out at night?" (the moon)

What your child can say or do

Your child might rename the family pet "Captain" and demand a cap. Salutes are acceptable at dinner; the cap can be paper.

Out in the real world

Sailors’ navy uniforms are worn by navies worldwide — US, UK, Canada, everywhere ships sail. The bow tie is the navy’s fancy cousin for land celebrations. Real night skies go navy before black — watch for it tonight.

Try it together

Captain says: "Captain says anchor your feet… Captain says scrub the deck… Captain says navy night!" Navy commands, sailor obedience, one shade drilled per round. Bedtime version ends with "lights to navy — goodnight."

Understanding check

Ask: "what is the recipe for navy?" (blue plus a little black) "What is navy named after?" (the sailors — the navy) "Show me the blue family: light blue, blue, NAVY." (three hands, three shades)

This lesson pairs with the Navy flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Colors & Shades.
